summary: Across the seven days from October 10 to 16, Miqyas logged 64 articles. Social coverage carried the heaviest negative weight: 34 of 64 social readings (53.1%) were negative, against 22 (34.4%) on the political axis and 12 (18.8%) on the economic axis. The social figure reflects a run of deadly incidents, not one storyline: a Houthi strike on Riyadh airport that Dawn reported killed a Pakistani national, a train derailment near Multan that killed at least five, the collapse of a school roof in Peshawar that killed a teacher and 32 students, and a shooting at an Oregon elementary school. Detentions also weighed on this axis. The family of Pakistan Awam Raj Tehreek chief Iqrar ul Hassan says he was taken from his home at night, while his lawyer says the NCCIA denied holding him and Punjab's information minister said police did not arrest him. Positive readings were scarce on every axis, just 10 of 192 category readings all week.

The week's dominant storyline was the emergency and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, which accounted for 18 of the 22 stories flagged for review. It moved fast: on October 10 unnamed sources said the Centre was weighing the step, on October 11 President Zardari approved the cabinet's decision under Articles 232 and 234, the army's deployment was then notified under Article 245, the Prime Minister set up an 11-member committee under Deputy PM Ishaq Dar, and on October 15 a joint sitting of Parliament ratified the measures after a procedural motion carried 214 to 56 amid opposition protests. Federal ministers say the step was driven by rising terrorism and the PTI-led provincial government's alleged withdrawal from counterterrorism work, with the law minister citing a 195 per cent rise in attacks. PTI, JUI-F, Jamaat-e-Islami and the TTAP opposition alliance reject it as an assault on the province's mandate, PTI says Chief Minister Sohail Afridi was arrested, and the Peshawar High Court is due to hear PTI's petitions on October 20. Security reporting formed the backdrop: ISPR said troops killed 12 militants, including Afghan Taliban personnel, in a foiled infiltration attempt in Kurram, with coverage citing PICSS data that militant attacks in September reached a 12-year monthly high. This one storyline explains much of the political negativity, and four of the week's 12 negative economic readings were attached to emergency coverage. The few economic positives came from Oman's foreign minister's visit (two cards), the Prime Minister's call for wider legal migration routes to Europe, and an apex court ruling limiting how long tax re-adjudication can take.

The political lean readings held up well given how polarising the week's main story was. Of 64 articles, 56 were rated balanced, 7 pro-government and 1 pro-opposition. Five of the seven pro-government readings were emergency stories built around one side speaking: Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari's speech paired with unnamed-source reports of emergency plans, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi's account of failed talks, the ministers' joint press conference, the law minister's briefing that the emergency covers the whole province, and Senator Faisal Vawda's remarks. The lone pro-opposition reading was the joint opposition's statement condemning the move. These tilted readings were split between Geo News and Dawn News, which suggests the tilt follows story format (a statement carried with no reply from the other side) more than any one publisher. Cards that combined two or three publications, such as the proclamation itself and the parliamentary ratification, were rated balanced.

Confidence was moderate for most of the week: 24 articles high, 38 medium and 2 low. Among flagged stories the reasons for medium or low ratings repeat: early emergency reports rested on unnamed sources (later events matched them), the Kurram account was carried by three publications but all relied on one ISPR statement, and several cards were built from RSS excerpts because the full page could not be fetched. Readers should treat specific figures this week, including the government's 195 per cent figure, PTI's arrest claims and the Cockroach Janta Party's claim that some 10,000 supporters were detained in India, as claims by the parties making them, not as verified facts.

notableStories.headline: Emergency, governor's rule imposed in KP as President Zardari approves summary on PM's advice
notableStories.context: The week's central development: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa was placed under emergency and governor's rule, which the government links to security conditions and which PTI and other parties called undemocratic and vowed to challenge in court.

notableStories.headline: Parliament's joint sitting ratifies emergency, governor's rule in KP
notableStories.context: Parliament gave its backing to the KP measures after a 214 to 56 procedural vote, while PTI and JUI-F lawmakers objected that no evidence was presented.

notableStories.headline: Soldier martyred, 12 terrorists killed as security forces foil infiltration attempt in Kurram: ISPR
notableStories.context: The security backdrop to the week, with ISPR reporting a deadly infiltration attempt from Afghanistan and coverage citing a 12-year monthly high in militant attacks in September.

notableStories.headline: Iqrar ul Hassan 'picked up' from home, whereabouts remain unknown: family
notableStories.context: A political party chief's family says he was taken from his home at night, while the NCCIA reportedly denied holding him and Punjab officials said police did not arrest him.

notableStories.headline: India's 'cockroach' movement chief detained ahead of major protest
notableStories.context: The week's main regional story: Indian police held the leader of a satirical party protesting a disputed voter roll revision, with the party claiming mass detentions that police have not addressed.
